transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CRE), Rachel Kim (CISO, Helio), Tom Novak (SRE Manager), Anya Vass (Compliance), Jared Cole (Platform Security)

Summary (auto-generated): Quick technical readout focusing on incident response playbooks, KMS integration for private deployments, and how Redwood's SLA and escalation maps to Helio's runbooks. Several follow-ups assigned.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we have Rachel, Tom, Anya and Jared from Helio, and Luis and I from Redwood. Does that sound right?
[00:08] Rachel Kim: Yep, that's right. Thanks for doing this. We wanted to validate your incident and BCDR flow before the exec review next month.
[00:15] Luis Ortega: Great, thanks. We'll try to be pragmatic — walk through a failover scenario, the KMS options for private, and how audit logs travel.
[00:22] Tom Novak: One thing up front — our SRE org has strict RTO targets for the payment gateway services, like 5 minutes for VIPs, 1 hour for backend batch jobs. We'll need to see how Redwood supports tiered RTO/RPO.
[00:33] Priya Desai: (muttering) that's tight but okay.
[00:36] Maya Patel: Totally. We'll map Redwood Dedicated vs Private behaviors and fallback plans. Quick note: some of the product names in my notes may be slightly off — apologies, speech transcription is funky — but we'll attach the exact doc links.

[00:50] Luis Ortega: I'll start with architecture. For private deployments you can run Redwood Private in your VPC or on-prem. KMS options: bring your own KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) via customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed envelopes. We support HSM-backed keys for FIPS requirements.
[01:05] Jared Cole: When you say "envelopes", you mean envelope encryption with the platform key wrapping customer keys? How is key rotation handled?
[01:12] Luis Ortega: Yes, envelope encryption. Rotation is supported, we recommend rotating CMKs every 90 days, and Redwood will rotate intermediate keys on a staggered schedule. We provide rotation tooling and audit logs for key ops.
[01:24] Anya Vass: Audit logs are critical for us. What's retention and can we get tamper-proofing? We have regulatory constraints to keep logs for seven years for certain flows.
[01:33] Maya Patel: Short answer: yes, you can export logs off-platform to your SIEM, we support immutable storage options, and we can extend retention via our log-archival integrations. We'll send the retention configuration matrix.
[01:45] Tom Novak: Is there support for streaming logs via Kafka or only S3 export?
[01:49] Luis Ortega: Both — we support event streaming to Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, and S3-based archival. The endpoint formats are JSON with consistent fields but note that some field names in early runtime versions were different — so we'd share the schema map.

[02:10] Rachel Kim: On the incident side — we need your escalation matrix. If the inference tier is degraded, how does Redwood notify us and what's your expected reaction time?
[02:20] Maya Patel: Our standard is alerting via PagerDuty integration with a four-tier escalation path: SE on-call -> Engagement lead -> Engineering on-call -> Exec on-call. For dedicated customers we can compress those windows and add 24/7 support. SLA typically defines initial response and time-to-ack.
[02:35] Tom Novak: Can you give concrete numbers? We can't present vague terms to our legal/compliance team.
[02:40] Maya Patel: Sure. For Dedicated customers with our premium SLA: initial acknowledgment within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 60 minutes, and either automated failover or capacity increase within 30 minutes of mitigation plan depending on the failure class. For hosted tier it's looser — ack within 60, plan within 4 hours. We'll provide the SLA table.
[02:59] Anya Vass: Penalty triggers? Credits?
[03:02] Maya Patel: Yes, credits are tiered based on per-incident downtime beyond the SLA windows. We'll attach the legal excerpt but discuss specifics in contracting.

[03:20] Luis Ortega: Walkthrough of a failover: imagine primary inference cluster in us-east. If latency rises above threshold or instance health fails, the router will attempt local autoscaling then fallback to a compatible model variant in another region or to a lower-cost quantized variant. For Helio's stricter RTOs, we recommend Dedicated pools with cross-zone redundancy and a warm standby in a second region.
[03:45] Tom Novak: Warm standby — what's the RPO there?
[03:48] Luis Ortega: With warm standby and KV cache replication it's sub-5 minutes for model state and near-zero token loss for stateless requests. For stateful chat sessions you should assume a small window where in-flight context must be rehydrated; we'll walk the team through KV checkpointing cadence.
[04:05] Rachel Kim: That token loss window worries compliance — can you guarantee encryption-in-flight and at-rest for those checkpoints?
[04:12] Luis Ortega: Yes, TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest. Checkpoints stored in your-managed bucket can be encrypted with your CMK.
[04:20] Jared Cole: Regarding SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM provisioning and group-based roles. Does Redwood support SCIM v2 and SAML 2.0?
[04:28] Priya Desai: quick yes, SCIM v2 and SAML 2.0 are supported. We also map SCIM groups to RBAC roles (admin, dev, view-only, auditor). There's an audit trail for role changes.
[04:40] Anya Vass: Can auditors get read-only access via a special role with restricted export? We prefer not to use service accounts with broad privileges.
[04:46] Maya Patel: You can create an "auditor" role w/ restricted API tokens scoped to read-only logs and evals. We also support time-bound credentials and token revocation to limit exposure.

[04:58] Tom Novak: On the runbook side, we want to run a 72-hour failover test across both Redwood Private and Dedicated to validate RTO/RPO. Who runs the failover and what's the rollback path?
[05:08] Luis Ortega: We usually run joint tabletop first, then an orchestrated test. Redwood SE will trigger failover steps with SRE on call, verify traffic cutover, and measure recovery. Rollback is symmetrical: fallback to primary cluster and reconcile KV state; we have reconciler tooling but stateful sessions may require reconciliation scripts.
[05:30] Rachel Kim: Are there any known gotchas? We need the failure modes spelled out.
[05:34] Priya Desai: small note — large batch jobs can lead to cold-cache scenarios where latency spikes until caches warm up; plan for canary warmup traffic. Also some older model kernels show different memory characteristics under 4k+ sequences — SEs will point to mitigation.
[05:49] Luis Ortega: yep, that's why we recommended tiering endpoints and using smaller context sizes for critical paths where possible. Also backing off to quantized variants can reduce memory but changes generation quality slightly — we'll run evals with your prompt sets.

[06:05] Anya Vass: About auditability: do you provide signed integrity proofs for logs? Tamper evidence?
[06:11] Luis Ortega: We offer cryptographic signing of log batches and a hash chain option for attestation, plus export to an immutable S3 bucket you control. For high assurance customers we can do HSM-backed signing.
[06:22] Jared Cole: For data residency, Helio has EU-only data for EU customers. Can Redwood guarantee that inference and logs remain in region?
[06:29] Maya Patel: Yes — for Private deployments in your VPC you control the region. For Hosted, we offer region pinning and ensure logs/data do not cross boundaries per config. We'll send the residency matrix.

[06:45] Tom Novak: One of our legal folks asked about forensic access during incidents — what access will Redwood grant and how quickly?
[06:52] Maya Patel: For Dedicated and Private, you can enable forensic access via time-limited session tokens and role escalation; Redwood's SRE will coordinate. Typical turnaround for a joint forensic bundle is 24-48 hours depending on scope. For hosted tier, we have defined procedures but sharing is more limited.
[07:08] Rachel Kim: Good — please include that in the pack.

[07:12] Luis Ortega: Quick demo note — we'll attach a sample runbook and the playbook for a cross-region failover.
[07:18] Maya Patel: Alright let's quickly capture the concrete next steps: Maya to send security pack, Luis to set up runbook + test plan, Tom to provide Helio SLOs and critical endpoints, Anya to confirm log retention/residency specifics.
[07:32] Rachel Kim: Thanks. One more Q — if we need HSM-backed KMS integrated into our private deployment, any licensing or extra cost?
[07:39] Maya Patel: There may be an add-on for HSM-backed key management and for accelerated SLAs. We'll include cost guidance in the follow-up.

[07:48] Tom Novak: Also, for the test, can Redwood provide a non-prod mirror with realistic load generator? We prefer a staging blast that emulates production traffic but isolated.
[07:57] Luis Ortega: Yes we can spin a temporary staging harness and share the load generator; we'll provide sample configs and synthetic workload scripts.

[08:10] Rachel Kim: Perfect. Any blockers today?
[08:13] Anya Vass: None from compliance if Redwood shares the attestation docs and retention matrix.
[08:18] Maya Patel: Great, we'll get that out this week. Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and book the tabletop.

End of transcript.

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors and speaker overlaps. Shared links during the call: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (attestations), https://redwood.example.com/runbook-samples (failover playbooks), spreadsheet for SLA table (link shared in chat).
